summary: Robert Maclagan worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Edinburgh, Addiscombe Military Seminary (~1837–1839), and the Royal School of Military Engineering (~1839–1840), later serving as Principal at IIT Roorkee (1847–1860).

Robert Magliola worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies after earning his Ph.D. at Princeton University (~1966–1970). He held posts at Purdue, Tamkang, Assumption, and Columbia universities, and was Distinguished Chair Professor at National Taiwan University (~1993–1998).

Robert Mayer works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Bristol (-1985) and earned his Ph.D. from Leiden University under Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen, later joining the University of Oxford faculty in 2002.

Robert Needham Cust worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Eton College, Trinity College Cambridge, East India Company College, Haileybury, and Fort William College, and served in the Bengal Civil Service (~1843–1867).

Robert P. Goldman is an Indologist who studied at Columbia and the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher, Shivram Dattatray Joshi, and others. He became a professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~1971).

Robert S. Ellwood specialized in religious studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Colorado, Yale University, and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade (~1964–1967), and held a post at the University of Southern California (~1967–1997).

Robert S. Nelson is a historian and archaeologist who studied at Rice University (~1965–1969) and New York University (~1971–1978). He served as professor at the University of Chicago (~1974–2005) and held a post at Yale University (~2005).

Robert S. P. Beekes specialized in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Leiden University (~1956–1969) under F. B. J. Kuiper, and held posts at Marnix Gymnasium as well as Leiden University (1973, 1979).
Robert Sewell was an Indologist and historian who served in the Indian Civil Service (~1868–1894) and held the post of Keeper at the Tamil Nadu Archives.
Robert Seymour Conway specialized in linguistics after studying at the City of London School (~1878–1883). He held posts at Newnham College (~1887–1893) and Gonville and Caius College (~1888–1894).
Robert Warren Clark works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under doctoral supervisor Karen Christina Lang (attested 1994) and adviser and teacher K. L. Seshagiri Rao.

Robert Zimmermann was an Indologist who studied at St Beuno's and completed his doctorate at the University of Berlin (1908–1913). He served as professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1914–1930), and was Leiter at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Robin Coningham is an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at King's College and the University of Cambridge under Raymond Allchin, and held professorships at the University of Bradford (1994–2005) and Durham University (2005).
Robin D. S. Yates is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (~1974–1980) and held a James McGill Professorship at McGill University (~1990).

Robin Dunbar studied at Magdalen College School, Magdalen College (~1966–1969), and completed his doctoral studies under John Crook (~1969–1974). He held a post at University College London (~1987–1994).

Roderick M. Chisholm was a philosopher who studied at Brown and Harvard universities. He held professorships at the Barnes Foundation (~1946) and Brown University (~1947–1987), served as Honorarprofessor at Graz (1974), and held posts at UMass Amherst and philosophical societies.
Roderick S. Bucknell was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held posts at the University of Queensland from ~1976 to 1990 and as Associate Professor from ~1991 to 2002.

Roderick Whitfield is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He was affiliated with the British Museum (attested 1986), the University of London (attested 2010), and SOAS University of London as professor emeritus (attested 2011, 2022).

Roger Bischoff works in Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Mother Sayamagyi and U Chit Tin, and served as an Assistant Teacher at the International Meditation Centre (attested 1995).
Roger Brown was a linguist who completed his studies at the University of Michigan (~1946–1952). He subsequently held a post at Harvard University from 1962 to 1994.
